Family of God
FAM-uh-lee uhv GOD
proper noun
The church as the household and family of God, His adopted children and one another’s brethren. Primary dual entry for the same reality: Spiritual Family / Household of God.

📖 Biblical Definition

The family of God is one of the great figures Scripture uses for the church—the household of God, His adopted children, brothers and sisters of one another and of Christ the elder Brother. Believers are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God; the church is the house of God, the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth. By adoption the redeemed are made sons: behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God. And being children of one Father, they are brethren one to another, charged to do good especially unto them who are of the household of faith. This family is not founded on flesh and blood but on the new birth and adoption in Christ; its bond is thicker than natural kinship, for the Lord said that whosoever does the will of His Father is His brother and sister and mother. The dictionary reads the family of God as the church in her warmth and nearness—the redeemed gathered into one household under one Father, made sons by adoption, brethren to one another, bound by a love and loyalty that the natural family only foreshadows—so that the lonely are set in families, the orphaned given a Father, and the believer brought into a people who are nearer than brothers, the household of God for ever.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The church as the household and family of God—His adopted children, brethren of one another and of Christ; a bond founded on the new birth, nearer than natural kinship.

📖 Key Scripture

Eph 2:19 — "Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;"

Gal 6:10 — "As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith."

1Ti 3:15 — "But if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth."

1Jo 3:1 — "Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The family of God is sentimentalized into mere belonging without holiness, or set against the natural family; rightly held, it is the household founded on the new birth, binding the redeemed in love and duty.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Two distortions touch the figure. The first sentimentalizes the family of God into mere belonging and acceptance without holiness—a warm fellowship that asks nothing of repentance, faith, or obedience, as though one were born into God’s family by good feeling rather than by the new birth and adoption in Christ. The second sets the family of God against the natural family, as if devotion to the church relieved one of the God-given duties to spouse, children, and parents. But Scripture honors both: the man who provides not for his own house has denied the faith, even as the church is the household of God.

The principle to recover is the family of God founded on the new birth and binding the redeemed in love and duty. The church is a true family—the household of God, His adopted sons, brethren of one another and of Christ—but a family entered not by flesh and blood nor by mere belonging, but by regeneration and adoption through faith in Christ. Its bond is real and weighty: believers are to do good especially to the household of faith, to bear one another’s burdens, to love as brethren. This family does not abolish the natural one but fulfills and outlasts it, gathering the lonely into a people and giving the orphaned a Father who will never leave them.
